page: Google Cloud Platform z4d-highmem-384-standardlssd-metal is a storage-optimized bare metal server powered by x86_64 architecture. The host is configured with 384 dedicated vCPUs and 3072.0 GB of RAM, providing a memory allocation of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Operating directly on bare metal hardware, it bypasses virtualization layers to eliminate hypervisor overhead.

The instance includes an extensive direct-attached storage setup featuring 12 local NVMe SSDs, yielding a total capacity of 45,097 GB. It does not include dedicated GPU accelerators, nor does it supply complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Combining high memory density with over 45 TB of local NVMe SSD capacity inside a bare metal footprint delivers significant resource consolidation on a single physical node. This resource profile is structured for high-performance enterprise databases, large-scale in-memory analytics, transactional database systems, and data-intensive ETL workloads.

This configuration fits high-performance database management systems, large in-memory transactional databases, big data analytics engines, and data warehousing workloads requiring substantial local IOPS and memory resources.
